BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against our playbook. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out

  SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses

**Project Kestrel: Seller package review against Buyer playbook**

I reviewed all 16 items. The Seller's "[STANDARD]" tags and "reviewer efficiency" note don't reduce the review: none of these terms has been agreed by us, and several conflict with the playbook. The Seller's market-context claims and "FINAL" label don't bind the Buyer. None of the Seller's positions is acceptable as drafted, and no fallback can be offered without written authority from Amelia Frost, which has not been given.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6.0m starting position. The 20% / AUD 4.8m fallback is usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at 25%/AUD 6.0m. Do not concede to 20% without written authority.
- **Reason:** The Seller's figure equals our conditional fallback, which has not been authorised.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000, recovering only the excess.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 first-dollar.
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are five times our de minimis and five times our basket, and the excess-only mechanic removes the first-dollar recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion, applying to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion for general claims. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" wording must not reach Fundamental/Title claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at 24 months and strike the "all Claims" override.
- **Reason:** The general time limit is a fallback item and the blanket override would cut across the separate Fundamental/Title regime.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright.
- **Reason:** Title and capacity are fundamental to what the Buyer is paying for, and folding them into the general regime is inconsistent with the playbook.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," with no fraud exception.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; insert the carve-out expressly.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the "any nature" wording removes protection against fraud, which is a non-negotiable playbook position.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records, plus Schedule 7.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; limit disclosure to specific, fairly disclosed matters.
- **Reason:** General data-room disclosure would hollow out every warranty, and the Disclosure Letter's own §1.4 and §11 provisions do not change this.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for matters the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; delete the clause.
- **Reason:** A blanket exclusion for anything discoverable would effectively negate the warranties and indemnities the Buyer is relying on, including the DD-006 and DD-010 matters the Buyer already knows about.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only; treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The disclosure confirms no final consent or condition evidence is included.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; make effective consent plus condition evidence a pre-Completion condition.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and consent-on-delivery leaves the consent unverified at Completion.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion." The disclosure confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release; require payout and release at Completion.
- **Reason:** Leaving AUD 3.2m of secured debt in place after Completion exposes the Buyer to the Company's secured obligations without a verified release.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** Bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The disclosure notes that AUD 420,000 in conditional bonuses is excluded from the draft funds flow and does not address payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item or funded by the Seller. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; add a specific line item for the bonuses and on-costs, Seller-funded.
- **Reason:** Silent exclusion would shift a known AUD 420,000 liability (plus unquantified on-costs) to the Buyer after Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate." The disclosure states that the AUD 180,000 open amount is not independently verified and that no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 figure is neither verified nor disputed; do not assert it is owed or paid.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity; broaden it and preserve the SOW3 cure.
- **Reason:** Ironquay's transfer conditions (DD-004 clause 7.3) depend on all SOW3 fees being cleared, which the Seller has not evidenced.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." The disclosure says the matter is not characterised as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** Preserve logs, investigate, and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation; require log preservation, investigation and updates before Completion.
- **Reason:** The file may contain about 1,240 personal records sent to an unintended address, and the investigation is unresolved, so the Seller cannot conclude it is immaterial.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable and accrued, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Assess the renewals before accepting the characterisation; do not treat them as Debt or deduct from price.
- **Reason:** The disclosure does not confirm whether the renewals are ordinary-course, terminable or accrued, so the ordinary-course label is unverified.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A "limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise," and the Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories are collapsed into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; restore separate categories and delete the blanket override.
- **Reason:** The Seller's override would silently apply general caps and time limits to categories that must sit outside them.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as sole evidence; require independent title and encumbrance searches and corporate authority evidence.
- **Reason:** The Seller's own register cannot verify that the Seller owns the shares it is selling.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" characterisation; keep the Tax and IP terms open and outside the general regime.
- **Reason:** Nothing in the package has agreed these terms, and placing them in the general regime would cap liability the Buyer has not agreed to limit.

---

**Overall:** No item is cleared. The Seller's package conflicts with the playbook on every SPA-N item. Any move toward the Seller's 20% cap or 18-month period requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and no such authority has been given.
